notes: Part counts match the 57-piece parts list. Wheels and tyres are separate pieces (4 wheels, 4 tyres).

Connectivity fix: every other_joins endpoint is now a plain piece id with the port names moved into the method text. Before, port-qualified ids such as 'b12:pin.1' left the wheels, tyres, exhaust wheel and flags as separate groups. The whole model is now one connected build.
The booklet pictures are small. The stacking in rests_on is my best reading, not exact stud positions, so check it against the booklet.
Steps 1-2: the 1x8 and 2x4 plates form the base, with the 2x2 wheel-holder plates at the rear (6157) and front (4600).
Step 7 builds two mirrored bracket + 1x2 slope sub-assemblies.
Step 8: the grey wheel 42610 goes on the pin of the 2x2 pin brick, as a rear exhaust.
Steps 13-14 add the four wheels: big balloon tyres on the 6157 rear holder, small tyres on the 4600 front holder.

Step 14 turns the model over. I read the grey round plate and the other leftover parts as an underside stack, attached with studs pushed up into the body's anti-studs. They have empty rests_on and are linked in other_joins instead.
The two black side-handle plates are held at the rear (b54, b55), each with a black flag clipped on. The flag's two clips both grip the single bar. Attachment points are assumed.
